dedupe_keys.name: western oc2 emulated 5g core packet capture and csv

description: Western OC2 Lab publishes packet-level data from an emulated 5G core network for studying NWDAF and network-function interactions. The public GitHub repository lists a PCAPNG capture and a CSV export. Its README says the capture includes initial UE registration and 138 minutes of subsequent operations. The CSV exposes packet sequence, emulation time, source and destination, protocol, byte length and information fields. A private IP map identifies functions such as AMF, SMF, UPF, gNB and UE in the single emulated topology. GitHub states MIT and the files are freely accessible. A telecom modeller could use the capture or CSV to characterize protocol mixes and packet exchanges for core-network traffic or capacity simulations. This is a lab emulation, not measured traffic from an operating network or a geographic coverage map. The calendar capture date, CSV row count and payload quality were not checked, and no files were downloaded. Related resources include the separate IIITV summary pipeline that processes this source. A further caveat is that packet times use local emulation time, not a verified UTC wall clock.
